newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine airport privatization still on - official.
newsitem.headline: Argentine airport privatization still on - official.

text.p: The Argentine government will appeal a judges ruling against the planned privatization of most of the country's airports and the sell-off will proceed as planned, a government official said Tuesday.

The government has still not been formally notified of the court decision, but when we are, we will appeal the ruling and it will be suspended. In other words, the privatization will not be delayed even by a second, said Jorge Rottemberg, chief advisor to Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez, quoted by the state-controlled Telam news agency.
A federal Argentine judge ruled earlier Tuesday that President Carlos Menem's decree to privatize the country's airports was void.
Menem finally approved the privatization of most of the country's main airports in June in a tender for a single, 30-year concession to be awarded in October.

An official in the office of Judge Liliana Heiland told Reuters that she wrote in her ruling: "The system implemented in the decree 375/97, which regulates the matter, manifestly exceeds the executive's powers."
Heiland was ruling on a court case brought by opposition politicians.
